# The boundary cases that do not hold yet.
#
# One case per line: the test's own name for it, a space, and why it is here.
# Everything not on this list must hold, and everything on it must still fail.
# CI checks both directions, which is what makes this a ledger rather than a
# list of excuses:
#
#   a case fails and is NOT here  →  a new break, on the commit that made it
#   a case holds and IS here      →  it was fixed; take it off, in that commit
#
# So the file can only shrink, and it cannot shrink quietly. That is the same
# discipline the generated reference already lives under: the gate is not that
# the number is small, it is that the number cannot move without somebody saying
# so in the same commit.
#
# Every line here is a finding from the external audit of 2026-08-24 (D45), and
# every one of them is fixed by P6-24. When this file has only comments left,
# the trust-boundary group is closed.

# shim/no-authentication came off on 2026-08-29 (P7-17/F2): the shim now mints a
# 256-bit token per process unless --insecure-no-token is typed, so the case
# holds and the ledger's own rule says its line goes in the commit that fixed it.
